description: Stereo comb filter built from twelve parallel bandpass filters, with a feedback path that can be sent out to another effect and brought back

params.text: Sets the frequency of the lowest of the twelve bands, -3 to 3 octaves around 130.8125Hz, the eleven above it landing at whole multiples of it
Sets the sharpness of all twelve bands together, 0 to 0.99, which becomes a filter Q of 4 up to about 48; it also lifts the output level to make up for what the filtering takes away
Sets how much of the comb's own output goes back into its input, 0 to 1, halved before it is applied
Fades the even-numbered bands against the odd-numbered ones, -1 to 1: one end leaves only the odd bands, the other only the even, and the centre passes both at half level
Pushes the eleven upper bands off the whole multiples of the lowest one, -1 to 1, which takes the comb out of tune and makes it more percussive

inputs.text: The left audio input, divided by 2.5 before the filters; with no cable this channel is silent and its feedback path carries nothing
The right audio input, divided by 2.5 before the filters; with no cable the right channel takes the left input, feedback and all
Clamped to -3V and 3V and added to the Cutoff knob at one volt per octave
The absolute value of the voltage divided by 10, clamped to 0.9, multiplies the Resonance knob; with no cable the knob is used on its own
Multiplies the Feedback knob; with no cable the knob is used on its own, and the voltage is not clamped, so a few volts here push the loop far past what the knob alone reaches
The return of the left feedback loop, added to the left input alongside the internal feedback; it is read only while the left Send jack also has a cable
The return of the right feedback loop, added to the right input alongside the internal feedback; it is read only while the right Send jack also has a cable
Divided by 5, clamped to -1 and 1, and multiplied by the Odd/Even knob; with no cable the knob is used on its own

outputs.text: The left comb sum after the drive stage, clamped to -5V and 5V
The right comb sum after the drive stage, clamped to -5V and 5V
The left comb sum before the drive stage, at 5V for full scale, meant to feed an effect whose output comes back to the left Return jack
The right comb sum before the drive stage, at 5V for full scale, meant to feed an effect whose output comes back to the right Return jack

notes: twelve bandpass filters run in parallel, the lowest one at the Cutoff frequency and the other eleven at multiples of it that the Skew knob can pull off true
the send and return path only runs when both the Send jack and the Return jack of that channel have cables; either one on its own does nothing
the internal feedback is added to the audio input, so with no cable in that channel's Input jack the filters cannot ring on their own
every jack is monophonic, whatever is patched in
